=============== requirements/aria-chart-role-img.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): add `role="img"` to chart container element'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Assistive technologies need a semantic hint that the chart container represents an image-like graphic region rather than an untyped generic element. Without that role, accessibility support is weaker even when aria labeling is enabled.


  ## Desired outcome

  Mark the chart container with `role="img"` so screen readers can interpret the rendered chart as a descriptive graphical object and pair it with the existing aria text more reliably.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A rendered chart container exposes `role="img"`, existing aria-label behavior continues to work on the same element, and visual rendering is unchanged.'
=============== requirements/aria-label-data-exclusion.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): allows excluding data in aria-label'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Accessible chart descriptions can become noisy when datasets include raw coordinates, identifiers, or helper columns that are meaningful for computation but not for screen-reader output. Authors need a way to omit specific dimensions while keeping the underlying data intact.


  ## Desired outcome

  Let aria label generation exclude selected dataset columns through `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, so spoken descriptions can focus on the meaningful values without mutating the actual series data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId` lists dimension indexes, those values are omitted from the generated aria label, the remaining values still appear in order, and reading back the series data shows it was not modified by aria generation.'
=============== requirements/aria-ssr-safety.yaml
title: 'fix(aria): avoid throwing error in SSR mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams using ECharts for server-side rendering or prerendered output expect accessibility features to be safe to enable outside the browser. Right now aria processing can throw in SSR environments because DOM-only behavior is assumed even when no browser element exists.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make aria support safe in SSR mode so enabling accessibility metadata does not crash chart generation when ECharts is rendered without a live browser DOM.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts configured with aria can be created in server-rendered environments without throwing, browser rendering keeps its current accessibility behavior, and the fix does not require users to disable aria as a workaround.'
=============== requirements/aria-test-20218.yaml
title: 'test(aria): fix test case of #20218'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The automated coverage for aria column exclusion needs to reflect the public option structure that users are supposed to configure. This is test-maintenance work, not a change to chart behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the regression test so it validates the supported public contract at `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, while keeping the existing user-facing aria behavior and data-integrity expectations unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The regression test exercises `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, still confirms excluded columns disappear from the generated aria label, still confirms source data is left untouched, and no runtime feature change is introduced by the test update itself.'
=============== requirements/axis-custom-values.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): add `customValues` option to customize axis tick/label positions'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors sometimes need ticks and labels at hand-picked positions rather than at the axis scale’s automatically generated stops, for example when highlighting irregular milestones or business-specific checkpoints. Today this usually requires workarounds that can desynchronize labels from ticks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Allow both axis ticks and axis labels to opt into explicit positions through `customValues`, so authors can declare the exact values to show while still using the normal axis rendering pipeline.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Providing `customValues` on the tick or label configuration renders marks at the requested values, time axes handle those custom positions correctly, and charts that rely on automatic tick generation keep their current behavior.'
=============== requirements/axis-ticks-grid-overflow.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix ticks overflowing grid area with dataZoom'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When dataZoom is applied, axis ticks near the visible edges can extend beyond the grid area and make a chart look visually broken even though the zoomed range itself is valid. Authors expect clipped or bounded ticks that stay inside the plotting region.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep axis ticks contained within the grid when dataZoom changes the visible window, so zoomed charts look clean at the edges instead of drawing tick marks outside the plot area.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After zooming, edge ticks no longer overflow beyond the grid boundary, normal axis-tick rendering is preserved inside the plot, and unaffected non-zoomed charts keep their current appearance.'
=============== requirements/bar-bordercolor-large-data.yaml
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'
=============== requirements/bigint-data-handling.yaml
title: 'fix(data): avoid crashing with BigInt values'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some chart authors pass data that includes JavaScript `BigInt` values from upstream business logic or preprocessing steps. Instead of gracefully interpreting or rejecting that input, ECharts can crash during value detection and parsing, taking down the whole chart render.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make data ingestion robust when `BigInt` values are present so charts no longer throw during value parsing, and users can either render supported numeric content or get normal downstream handling instead of a hard crash.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supplying data that contains `BigInt` no longer causes an immediate exception in the parsing pipeline, and other supported numeric data paths continue to behave exactly as before.'
=============== requirements/boxplot-encode-category-axis.yaml
title: 'fix(boxplot): correctly handle `series.encode` with category axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Boxplot charts can be driven from datasets and `series.encode`, but when a category axis is involved the encoded dimensions may be interpreted incorrectly. The result is a valid option that renders with misplaced or missing statistical boxes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make boxplot series honor `series.encode` correctly on category axes so dataset-driven configurations map categories and box statistics to the intended dimensions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A boxplot backed by dataset plus `series.encode` renders the expected categories and box values on a category axis, the encoded mapping no longer breaks the series, and existing boxplots without encode keep their current behavior.'
=============== requirements/calendar-label-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(calendar): add `silent` option for `dayLabel`/`monthLabel`/`yearLabel`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using the calendar coordinate system may want the day, month, or year labels to serve as static annotation rather than interactive elements. Today those labels still participate in pointer interaction, which can interfere with hover behavior on the actual calendar data and make embedded dashboards feel unexpectedly clickable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calendar label interaction should be configurable independently for `dayLabel`, `monthLabel`, and `yearLabel`. When a user sets `silent: true` on any of those label configs, the corresponding rendered text should ignore pointer events while preserving the existing visual styling and positioning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can set `dayLabel.silent`, `monthLabel.silent`, and `yearLabel.silent` directly in the calendar option, and each one takes effect on its own. With `silent: true`, the label remains visible but no longer behaves like an interactive graphic element; with the option omitted or false, existing behavior stays unchanged.

  '
=============== requirements/candlestick-non-normal-states.yaml
title: 'fix(candlestick): add back missing support for non-normal states since v5.0.0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts support emphasis, blur, and select-style visual states, and users expect those non-normal states to continue working consistently across major versions. Since v5.0.0 some of that state handling was lost, so interactive styling no longer responds correctly.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore the missing non-normal state support for candlestick series so hover, selection, and related state-based visuals behave again the way chart authors expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Candlestick items respond correctly in non-normal states, state-specific styling takes effect again without breaking normal rendering, and existing candlestick options keep their prior semantics.'
=============== requirements/custom-renderitem-compoundpath.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'
=============== requirements/custom-series-installer.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): use installer for reusable custom series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Reusable custom series should integrate like other chart types so wrapper libraries and modular builds can register them through the standard installation flow. This is an API ergonomics improvement for developers building on top of ECharts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide installer-based registration for reusable custom series so they can be added through the normal modular setup path rather than special-case wiring.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reusable custom series can be registered through the standard installer flow, modular imports stay consistent with other chart features, and existing custom-series usage keeps working.'
=============== requirements/dark-legend-page-text.yaml
title: 'fix(theme): fix legend page text color in dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, legend pagination text can retain an incorrect color that reduces contrast and readability against the theme background. Users experience this as a theme inconsistency in otherwise polished dark dashboards.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix dark-theme legend page text coloring so paged legends remain readable and visually consistent with the rest of the dark theme.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Legend page text in dark mode uses an appropriate readable color, pagination controls stay visible against the dark background, and light-theme behavior is unchanged.'
=============== requirements/datazoom-handlelabel-show.yaml
title: 'feat(dataZoom): new option handleLabel.show'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Slider dataZoom handles can show useful value text while users interact, but some applications want those handle labels visible even outside active dragging or emphasis states. At the moment authors cannot explicitly control that visibility.


  ## Desired outcome

  Introduce `handleLabel.show` for slider dataZoom so teams can decide whether the handle labels are visible in the normal state, while `emphasis.handleLabel.show` continues to control the emphasized or dragging state separately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting `handleLabel.show` toggles normal-state handle-label visibility, `emphasis.handleLabel.show` governs the emphasized state, and existing slider behavior is preserved when the new option is left unset.'
=============== requirements/datazoom-movehandler-cursor.yaml
title: 'fix(dataZoom): change moveHandler cursor to default'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The move handle in dataZoom currently presents a cursor that implies a stronger drag affordance than the interaction actually intends in that state. This creates small but noticeable UX inconsistency in the control.


  ## Desired outcome

  Use the default cursor for the move handler so pointer feedback matches the intended interaction model without changing the rest of dataZoom behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Hovering the move handler shows the default cursor, dragging behavior stays available where it was before, and no other slider handle cursor states regress.'
=============== requirements/forked-workflow-deps.yaml
title: 'chore(workflow): use forked workflow deps for timely update'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  Project maintainers need the CI workflows that power preview and maintenance tasks to stay updateable without waiting on external bottlenecks. This is internal release-engineering work rather than a user-facing feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Adjust the workflow dependency source so maintainers can receive updates in a timely way while keeping the observable behavior of preview-related automation unchanged for contributors.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The workflows continue to run with the replacement dependency source, update cadence is no longer blocked in the old path, and no charting API or runtime behavior changes for users.'
=============== requirements/gauge-negative-z2.yaml
title: 'fix(gauge): fix z2 is negative when maxVal is negative'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Gauge charts may calculate drawing order from the maximum value, and when that maximum is negative the resulting `z2` can become negative as well. Users see this as incorrect stacking or visibility problems even though negative-value gauges are a legitimate configuration.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make gauge rendering robust for negative maxima so internal z-ordering stays valid and the gauge remains visible and layered correctly.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A gauge configured with a negative max value renders without hidden or mislayered elements, `z2` no longer falls into an invalid negative ordering state, and positive-value gauges behave as before.'
=============== requirements/geojson-region-styling-2.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors need region defaults embedded in GeoJSON to work consistently whether they use a standalone `geo` component or a `series.map`, and whether or not they explicitly list every region in `data` or `regions`. The initial GeoJSON styling support still leaves gaps in those map-series flows, especially when a region only exists in the source map and not in user-supplied series data.

  ## Desired outcome

  GeoJSON-defined region styling should become a first-class default across map usage, not just a geo-view special case. If a feature provides `properties.echartsStyle`, that style should flow into both `geo.regions` and `series.map` region models, including regions that need to be synthesized into the data so name-based lookup, rendering, and labels all remain complete.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A `series.map` can pick up `properties.echartsStyle` from the original GeoJSON even when the author did not manually add a matching data item for that region. The style participates in the normal region model pipeline instead of being a one-off view patch, so map rendering, labels, and region lookup stay consistent with other region options.

  '
=============== requirements/geojson-region-styling.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams who maintain their own GeoJSON files often want the map source itself to carry default presentation rules for specific regions, instead of forcing every chart option to restate those styles. At the moment, styling embedded directly in the GeoJSON is ignored, which makes shared map assets harder to reuse across multiple visualizations.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a GeoJSON region includes an `echartsStyle` property in its feature properties, ECharts should treat that as the region''s default styling for geo rendering. This should let authors ship map-specific visual defaults inside the original GeoJSON while still allowing chart configuration to build on top of those defaults where appropriate.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Region-level styles declared in GeoJSON `properties.echartsStyle` are reflected when the map is rendered through geo-based views, without requiring duplicate style configuration in every chart option. Existing GeoJSON files that do not define `echartsStyle` continue to render exactly as before.

  '
=============== requirements/georoam-totalzoom-event.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): add `totalZoom` parameter for the `georoam` event'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Applications that react to map zooming often need the cumulative zoom level, not just the latest roam gesture, in order to coordinate labels, overlays, or linked views. Today a `georoam` listener can detect that roaming happened but cannot directly read the total scale after repeated zoom operations.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose the accumulated zoom ratio on the `georoam` event as `totalZoom` so integrators can base follow-up UI logic on the map’s current effective zoom level instead of reconstructing it themselves.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A `georoam` handler receives `totalZoom` after zoom interactions, the value tracks cumulative zoom state across successive operations, and existing roam event behavior continues to work for listeners that do not use the new field.'
=============== requirements/inversed-time-bandwidth.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix bar bandWidth with inversed time axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Bar charts on an inversed time axis can calculate the wrong `bandWidth`, which causes bar sizing and spacing to look off even when the input data and axis configuration are otherwise correct. Authors experience this as distorted geometry on a valid timeline chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct bar bandwidth calculation for inversed time axes so bar width matches the actual axis interval direction and the rendered bars keep sensible spacing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars on an inversed time axis render with the expected width, reversing the axis no longer distorts band sizing, and non-inversed time-axis bar charts keep their current layout.'
=============== requirements/legend-action-isolation.yaml
title: 'fix(legend): fix legend action is not isolated from other legend components'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pages can contain multiple legend components, and actions intended for one legend should not silently affect another. Right now some legend operations leak across legend instances, causing unexpected selection changes elsewhere in the same chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Isolate legend actions so each legend component responds only to the interactions and action payloads meant for it, even when several legends coexist in one option.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Triggering an action on one legend no longer changes unrelated legend components, targeted legend interaction still works, and existing single-legend charts behave the same as before.'
=============== requirements/line-memory-reduction.yaml
title: 'perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Large line charts can put unnecessary pressure on the browser by holding more runtime memory than the renderer actually needs. Users feel this as slower interaction or higher memory usage rather than as a visible API problem.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reduce the runtime memory footprint of line-series rendering without changing chart appearance, public options, or event behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent line charts consume less memory during rendering or interaction, visual output remains unchanged, and no public configuration changes are required from chart authors.'
=============== requirements/linked-data-npe.yaml
title: 'fix(series): avoid NPE caused by `seriesData.getLinkedData`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Advanced charts and extensions can interact with linked data structures internally, but some series configurations hit a null-path and throw when linked data is absent. Users experience this as a broken render caused by an internal assumption rather than an invalid option they knowingly supplied.


  ## Desired outcome

  Harden series processing so code paths that consult `seriesData.getLinkedData` tolerate missing linked datasets and continue rendering safely instead of raising a null-pointer-style exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Series configurations that previously crashed due to missing linked data now render or degrade normally, no exception is thrown from the linked-data lookup path, and unaffected series behavior stays the same.'
=============== requirements/map-regions-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(map): support `regions[].silent` and update map data in tests'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Map authors sometimes need a region to remain visible but non-interactive, for example when a background territory should not respond to hover, selection, or tooltip behavior. ECharts already supports top-level `silent` behavior, but there is no reliable per-region contract for map and geo regions, so authors cannot selectively disable interaction on individual areas.

  ## Desired outcome

  Region configuration should support `silent` at the per-region level through `regions[].silent`, and that setting should be honored for both geo-based maps and `series.map` rendering. A region marked silent should keep its visual appearance while opting out of event handling and interactive affordances, without forcing the entire map to become non-interactive.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can declare `silent` on individual entries in `regions`, and the targeted region becomes non-interactive while neighboring regions continue to respond normally. The contract applies consistently to rendered GeoJSON regions and SVG-backed regions, and map data refreshes should preserve the updated region behavior instead of losing it when the source map data changes.

  '
=============== requirements/marker-formatter-series-context.yaml
title: 'fix(marker): fix marker label formatter can''t get series information'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When chart authors customize marker labels with formatter callbacks, they expect to receive the same series context that other formatter-based APIs expose. For mark points, lines, and areas, that context can currently be incomplete, which prevents formatter logic from reliably reading series information.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure marker label formatter callbacks receive the related series metadata consistently so custom label text can depend on the originating series without hacks or duplicated state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A marker label formatter can read the expected series information when building label text, the callback contract is consistent across marker types, and existing marker rendering remains unchanged when no custom formatter is used.'
=============== requirements/markline-symboloffset-2d-array.yaml
title: 'fix(type): markLine `symbolOffset` can be a 2d array for both symbols'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users configuring mark lines may want separate offsets for the symbols at each end, but the current type definition can reject valid configurations even though the renderer supports them. This creates unnecessary friction in strongly typed projects.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the public type contract so markLine `symbolOffset` accepts a 2D array when authors need to specify offsets for both symbols independently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  TypeScript accepts markLine configurations where `symbolOffset` is expressed as separate offset pairs for the two end symbols, existing simpler `symbolOffset` forms remain valid, and runtime chart behavior is unchanged.'
=============== requirements/master-into-v6.yaml
title: 'chore: merge master into v6'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The v6 release branch needs regular synchronization with ongoing master development so maintainers can keep packaging, fixes, and infrastructure aligned. This is branch-management work, not a new user-visible feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Merge the relevant master changes into the v6 branch while preserving the expected public behavior of the release line and avoiding regressions introduced by branch drift.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The v6 branch reflects the intended upstream updates, the merge does not invent a new standalone feature requirement of its own, and user-facing behavior is whatever the merged source already defines.'
=============== requirements/minmax-sampling-behavior.yaml
title: 'fix(sample): fix minmax sampling behaviour'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users relying on `minmax` sampling expect the downsampled line to preserve the local extrema from each interval. In some cases the current behavior picks the wrong points, so the sampled chart misrepresents the highs and lows of the underlying data.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix `minmax` sampling so the reduced series preserves the intended minimum and maximum behavior within each sampling bucket, especially around edge cases where the previous logic selected the wrong point order or values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A line using `minmax` sampling retains the visible peaks and troughs expected from the source data, the sampled output is stable in the previously failing scenario, and other sampling modes continue to behave as before.'
=============== requirements/npm-package-ignore-files.yaml
title: 'chore: ignore some unused dirs and files from npm'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Package consumers install ECharts from npm and only need the distributable assets required to use or bundle the library. Extra repository-only folders in the published package add noise and increase install size without adding user value.


  ## Desired outcome

  Tighten the npm package contents so development-only material that is not needed by downstream users is left out, while the package continues to install and work exactly the same for chart authors.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The published package excludes unnecessary repo artifacts, npm installs stay smaller and cleaner, and existing runtime and type-consumption behavior is unchanged for consumers.'
=============== requirements/pictorial-zero-value-flipping.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorial): fix zero value flipping for different axes'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using `pictorialBar` with image or path symbols expects zero-valued items to stay visually anchored without suddenly mirroring in the wrong direction. After the earlier zero-value fix, some axis combinations still render a flipped symbol when the chart changes between horizontal and vertical layouts or uses inverse axes, so the same data can look wrong depending on orientation.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-valued pictorial bars should keep a stable, sensible symbol direction across horizontal and vertical charts, including inverse-axis layouts. A value of zero must no longer trigger an accidental flip simply because the axis orientation or inversion changes.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The zero-value rendering is correct for all four combinations covered by chart authors in practice: horizontal, horizontal with inverse axis, vertical, and vertical with inverse axis. Non-zero pictorial bars continue to render with their existing direction logic, and the fix applies equally to custom image symbols and path-based symbols.

  '
=============== requirements/pictorialbar-zero-symbol-flip.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorialBar): symbol should not flip with zero data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pictorial bar charts can use symbol direction and orientation to express meaning, but a zero value should not invert that symbol unexpectedly. Right now hitting zero can flip the symbol, producing a misleading visual jump at exactly the point where no bar should extend.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep pictorial-bar symbols from flipping when the data value is zero so orientation stays stable across zero-valued points.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A zero-value pictorial bar preserves the expected symbol direction, nearby positive or negative values still render with their intended orientation rules, and zero no longer introduces a special-case flip.'
=============== requirements/pie-empty-circle-endangle.yaml
title: 'fix(pie): fix `endAngle` is not applied on the empty circle'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using a pie or half-donut chart can set `endAngle` to render only part of the ring, but when the series has no data and ECharts falls back to the empty-circle placeholder, that placeholder still behaves like a full circle instead of respecting the configured sweep. This makes dashboards look inconsistent whenever a dataset is temporarily empty.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a pie series renders its empty-circle state, the placeholder should honor the same `endAngle` setting that a normal pie would use so partial-ring designs keep their intended shape even with no slices to draw.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A chart configured with a non-default `endAngle` shows the empty circle with the matching arc extent rather than a full ring, and switching between empty and non-empty data keeps the visual geometry consistent.'
=============== requirements/pie-label-visibility.yaml
title: 'fix(pie): fix some labels may not show'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie charts with dense labels can occasionally hide labels that should remain visible, causing important categories to disappear from the rendered result even though there is enough room for them in the final layout. Authors experience this as an intermittent labeling bug rather than a configuration mistake.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct the pie-label layout logic so labels that should be shown are not incorrectly dropped during collision handling or final positioning.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The previously missing pie labels render consistently in the affected layout, other overlap-avoidance behavior still works, and unchanged configurations do not gain stray duplicate labels.'
=============== requirements/polar-coordinate-clipping.yaml
title: 'fix(polar): fix unexpected clipping in polar coordinate'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Charts in polar coordinates can clip content that should remain visible, producing truncated graphics near the edges even when the data and series configuration are valid. Authors see this as unexpected cropping rather than an intentional bound.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix polar-coordinate clipping so series content is only clipped where it should be, and valid shapes are not cut off unexpectedly by the rendering bounds.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected polar chart renders without the unwanted clipping artifact, legitimate boundary clipping still works where necessary, and non-polar charts are unaffected.'
=============== requirements/pt-br-translation.yaml
title: 'feat(i18n): improve pt-BR translation'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Portuguese-speaking users in Brazil rely on translated chart vocabulary for toolbox text, series names, and other built-in UI strings. Inaccurate or unnatural Brazilian Portuguese makes those interfaces feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  Improve the pt-BR translation so built-in chart text reads naturally for Brazilian Portuguese users while preserving the meaning of the original UI strings.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected built-in labels use the revised pt-BR wording, Portuguese-Brazil locale output is more accurate, and other locales remain unchanged.'

--- .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: Node CI

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]

concurrency:
  # Note that the `teardown-pr-preview` workflow needs the same group name
  # to cancel the running `ci` workflows
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x]

    steps:
      - name: Fetch commit count
        env:
          PR_COMMIT_COUNT: ${{ github.event.pull_request.commits }}
        run: |
          echo "FETCH_DEPTH=$(($PR_COMMIT_COUNT + 1))" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: ${{ env.FETCH_DEPTH }}

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        id: cache-dep
        uses: actions/cache@v3
        env:
          cache-name: cache-node-modules
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-lint-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cache-dep.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Collect changed files
        run: |
          mkdir ~/tmp/
          git diff ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} ${{ github.sha }} --diff-filter=ACM --name-only --relative '*src/**/*.ts' > ~/tmp/changed_files
          echo -e "Changed files: \n$(cat ~/tmp/changed_files)"

      - name: Lint
        run: npx eslint $(cat ~/tmp/changed_files)

      - name: Check types
        run: npm run checktype

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        id: cache-dep
        uses: actions/cache@v3
        env:
          cache-name: cache-node-modules
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-build-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cache-dep.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Unit Test
        run: npm run test

      - name: Build release
        run: npm run release

      - name: Test generated DTS
        run: npm run test:dts

      - name: Pack npm tarball
        if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'apache' }}
        id: pack-tarball
        run: |
          export PR_PREVIEW_DIR='echarts-pr-preview'
          mkdir -p $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          npm pack -pack-destination $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          echo "PR_PREVIEW_DIR=$PR_PREVIEW_DIR" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Save PR metadata and dist files
        if: ${{ steps.pack-tarball.outcome == 'success' }}
        id: save-pr-data
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          PR_COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PR_PREVIEW_DIR: ${{ env.PR_PREVIEW_DIR }}
        run: |
          cd $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          echo $PR_NUMBER > ./pr_number
          echo $PR_COMMIT_SHA > ./pr_commit_sha
          find . -type f -regex ".*\.tgz" -exec tar xvzf {} \;
          rm -f *.tgz
          echo -e "Dist files: \n$(ls -l)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: ${{ steps.save-pr-data.outcome == 'success' }}
        with:
          name: pr_preview
          path: ${{ env.PR_PREVIEW_DIR }}
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error

--- .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml
name: Deploy PR Preview

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Node CI']
    types: [completed]

jobs:
  on-success:
    if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'apache' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Determine if workflow build job is successful
        id: check-build-success
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          result-encoding: string
          script: |
            const jobsRes = await github.rest.actions.listJobsForWorkflowRun({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              run_id: context.payload.workflow_run.id
            });
            return jobsRes.data.jobs.some((job) => job.name.includes('build') && job.conclusion === 'success');

    outputs:
      SHOULD_DEPOLY: ${{ steps.check-build-success.outputs.result }}

  deploy:
    needs: [on-success]
    if: ${{ needs.on-success.outputs.SHOULD_DEPOLY == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Install action dependencies
        run: |
          mkdir .actions
          cd .actions
          git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/dawidd6/action-download-artifact.git
          git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/actions-cool/maintain-one-comment.git

      - name: Fetch PR dist files
        uses: ./.actions/action-download-artifact
        with:
          workflow: ${{ github.event.workflow.id }}
          run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: pr_preview
          if_no_artifact_found: fail

      - name: Output PR metadata
        id: pr-metadata
        run: |
          echo "NUMBER=$(cat pr_number)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "COMMIT_SHA=$(cat pr_commit_sha)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "COMMIT_SHA_SHORT=$(cat pr_commit_sha | cut -c 1-7)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy dist files
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.NUMBER }}
          SURGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SURGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          export SURGE_DOMAIN=https://echarts-pr-$PR_NUMBER.surge.sh
          npx surge --project ./package --domain $SURGE_DOMAIN --token $SURGE_TOKEN

      - name: Create comment for PR preview
        uses: ./.actions/maintain-one-comment
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.NUMBER }}
          COMMIT_SHA_SHORT: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.COMMIT_SHA_SHORT }}
        with:
          body: |
            <!-- ECHARTS_PR_PREVIEW -->
            The changes brought by this PR can be previewed at: https://echarts.apache.org/examples/editor?version=PR-${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}@${{ env.COMMIT_SHA_SHORT }}
          body-include: '<!-- ECHARTS_PR_PREVIEW -->'
          number: ${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}
--- .github/workflows/source-release.yml
name: Source Release

on:

jobs:

            --rcversion ${{env.RELEASE_VERSION}} \

      # Get RELEASE_NOTE.txt and pack it into zip.
      - name: Download materials
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v3

            LICENSE

  validate-source:

jobs:

        run: |

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        id: cache-dep
        uses: actions/cache@v3
        env:
          cache-name: cache-node-modules
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-lint-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies

        run: npm ci

      - name: Collect changed files
        run: |
          mkdir ~/tmp/
          git diff ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} ${{ github.sha }} --diff-filter=ACM --name-only --relative '*src/**/*.ts' > ~/tmp/changed_files
          echo -e "Changed files: \n$(cat ~/tmp/changed_files)"

      - name: Lint

      - name: Check types

      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules

          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-build-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cache-dep.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Unit Test
        run: npm run test

      - name: Build release
        run: npm run release

      - name: Test generated DTS
        run: npm run test:dts

      - name: Pack npm tarball
        if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'apache' }}

--- .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml
name: Deploy PR Preview

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Node CI']
    types: [completed]

jobs:
  on-success:
    if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'apache' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Determine if workflow build job is successful
        id: check-build-success
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          result-encoding: string
          script: |
            const jobsRes = await github.rest.actions.listJobsForWorkflowRun({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              run_id: context.payload.workflow_run.id
            });
            return jobsRes.data.jobs.some((job) => job.name.includes('build') && job.conclusion === 'success');

    outputs:
      SHOULD_DEPOLY: ${{ steps.check-build-success.outputs.result }}

  deploy:
    needs: [on-success]
    if: ${{ needs.on-success.outputs.SHOULD_DEPOLY == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Install action dependencies
        run: |
          mkdir .actions
          cd .actions
          git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/dawidd6/action-download-artifact.git
          git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/actions-cool/maintain-one-comment.git

      - name: Fetch PR dist files
        uses: ./.actions/action-download-artifact
        with:
          workflow: ${{ github.event.workflow.id }}
          run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: pr_preview
          if_no_artifact_found: fail

      - name: Output PR metadata
        id: pr-metadata
        run: |
          echo "NUMBER=$(cat pr_number)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "COMMIT_SHA=$(cat pr_commit_sha)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "COMMIT_SHA_SHORT=$(cat pr_commit_sha | cut -c 1-7)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy dist files
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.NUMBER }}
          SURGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SURGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          export SURGE_DOMAIN=https://echarts-pr-$PR_NUMBER.surge.sh
          npx surge --project ./package --domain $SURGE_DOMAIN --token $SURGE_TOKEN

      - name: Create comment for PR preview
        uses: ./.actions/maintain-one-comment
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.NUMBER }}
          COMMIT_SHA_SHORT: ${{ steps.pr-metadata.outputs.COMMIT_SHA_SHORT }}
        with:
          body: |
            <!-- ECHARTS_PR_PREVIEW -->
            The changes brought by this PR can be previewed at: https://echarts.apache.org/examples/editor?version=PR-${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}@${{ env.COMMIT_SHA_SHORT }}
          body-include: '<!-- ECHARTS_PR_PREVIEW -->'
          number: ${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}
